messages:
anya: quick heads-up — noticed a weird inconsistency in a canary handoff this morning, small but reproducible on my machine
anya: after a prefix eviction + remote handoff, some requests return stale value for ~30s then correct themselves (no errors)
miguel: can you paste the logs? do we see lease release + apply order mismatch?
anya: pasted minimal log below, timestamps are local:
```
2026-03-19T09:12:03Z shard-42 HANDOFF start key_prefix=org/123/
2026-03-19T09:12:03Z shard-42 eviction mark prefix=org/123/seq=987
2026-03-19T09:12:03Z shard-43 HANDOFF receive prefetch_ok
2026-03-19T09:12:03Z shard-42 lease release token=0x2b
2026-03-19T09:12:04Z shard-43 apply seq=988 key=org/123/a -> value=v2
2026-03-19T09:12:33Z shard-43 read key=org/123/a -> value=v1 (stale)
2026-03-19T09:12:35Z shard-43 read key=org/123/a -> value=v2 (correct)
```

anya: the weird part is reads after apply still briefly return the old value (v1) before flipping to v2
miguel: hmm. that smells like a visibility window where a read path is served from a local read cache that wasn't invalidated by the handoff event
kevin: could be double-caching: per-shard prefix cache + per-core read cache. If invalidation is best-effort, races can show stale results for short windows
sara: if this reproduces locally, can we add a smoke test that asserts read-after-handoff < X ms? we should detect regressions early
miguel: agreed. propose two things: 1) a deterministic smoke test in `eng-runtime/test/handoff_smoke.py` that forces eviction+handoff and samples reads; 2) metrics and a lightweight invariant check in runtime to count visibility mismatches when detected in debug builds
anya: love it. rough test sketch:
```
# pseudo
kv = connect_local_shards(2)
kv.write('org/123/a', 'v1')
kv.pin_prefix('org/123/')
kv.write('org/123/a', 'v2')
trigger_evict_and_handoff(prefix='org/123/')
for i in range(100):
  r = kv.read('org/123/a')
  record(r)
  sleep(10ms)
assert majority(records) == 'v2' within 1s
```

kevin: for metrics add:
- `kv.handoff.visibility_mismatch.count` (tag: env, shard_from, shard_to)
- `kv.handoff.visibility_mismatch.latency_ms` histogram
- `kv.handoff.handoff_duration_ms` gauge
these let us alert if mismatches > threshold in prod canary
sara: minor nit: don't call it "gauge" for duration — histogram or summary is better for latency
miguel: good catch. I'll use histogram for latency. Also add `kv.handoff.debug.invariant_violation` counter only enabled in debug builds (off in prod)
anya: implementation idea: when a handoff apply completes, emit a fence token T. Any reader that served a value older than the expected seq should increment the mismatch counter with token and seq info (strip PII)
kevin: that requires readers to check their served seq vs latest seen seq. cheap check: store a per-request observed-seq header and compare to `handoff.latest_seq(prefix)` if available
prefetch-bot: CI check queued: handoff-smoke-tests (linux, py37) #42
infra-bot: build/ci handoff-smoke-tests passed in 3m12s (flake: 1) :white_check_mark:
miguel: nice. next: rollout plan — enable metric collection for 5% of dedicated traffic + 100% of canaries (we have canary pool for handoffs). If mismatch spikes, auto-disable handoffs for that shard group
sara: add an alert: if `kv.handoff.visibility_mismatch.count` > 50 in 5m for any shard, page oncall and rollback canary
anya: also add a small `--handoff-sanity` runtime flag that enables an active verifier: after apply, do a quick read with strong consistency check (expensive, opt-in). We can turn it on for 1% of requests in prod for a week
kevin: can we make the verifier opportunistic and bounded (timeout 200ms) to avoid tail latency blowups?
miguel: yes — timeout 200ms, and sample 1% of handoffs. record verdicts in histogram; fail open (don't stop apply)
anya: quick PR checklist: 1) smoke test + CI job, 2) metrics + histogram, 3) invariant counter (debug-only), 4) runtime `--handoff-sanity` flag + sampler, 5) alert rule and runbook update
sara: assign owners? miguel: metrics + runtime flag. kevin: verifier implementation + sampling. anya: smoke test + runbook draft. I'll update the canary rollout doc with thresholds
prefetch-bot: test run results: handoff-smoke-tests flaky on macos, passing on linux
infra-bot: scheduled canary rollout job (group: handoff-sanity-1pct) for 2026-03-20T02:00:00Z
anya: thanks all. I'll push the initial smoke test PR tonight and tag you for review @miguel @kevin @sara :thumbsup:
miguel: thx — if anyone hits reproduction steps, post exact `kvtool` command and `GODEBUG`/env flags used
kevin: one more thought — add a small unit that validates that eviction completely clears in-memory prefix snapshots before releasing lease token. if that check fails in debug build, crash-fast so we can catch root cause early
sara: +1 crash-fast in debug, but don't ship that to prod. add a build tag `debug_handoff_checks`
anya: noted. will include in PR.
